ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • 4-day history of severe, persistent headache followed by subjective fever; recent travel to Thailand with multiple mosquito bites.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Headache began first; fever developed afterwards. Symptoms ongoing for 4 days, not improving with self-care.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat: no tightness, swelling, dysphagia, odynophagia, drooling, or voice change reported.
  • Nasal/ocular: no rhinorrhea, nasal obstruction, conjunctival symptoms, or photophobia.
  • Respiratory: no stridor, noisy breathing, or dyspnea.
  • Facial/oral swelling: none.
  • Otologic: no ear pain or hearing changes.
  • Neck: no neck stiffness; able to move neck freely.
- Other systemic features:
  • Generalized myalgia, feels cold but no rigors.
  • Diffuse red, pruritic rash; blanching on glass test.
  • No nausea, vomiting, cough, focal neurologic deficit, or pins & needles.
- Relevant past episodes/treatments:
  • None reported.
- Allergies:
  • Denies drug or food allergies.
- Current medications:
  • Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  • No regular prescription medications.
- Social context:
  • Patient alone during video call; no mention of accompaniment at home.

Objective:
- Observable findings (video):
  • Rash described verbally as generalized red, itchy, blanching; visual confirmation not documented.
  • No visible facial, lip, tongue, or neck swelling noted by clinician.
- Airway/breathing: No reported/observed stridor or respiratory distress.
- Mental status: Alert, oriented, able to engage in conversation.
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination details: Full physical exam not performed (tele-consult only).
- Accompaniment: None stated.

Assessment:
- Undifferentiated febrile illness with headache, myalgia, and blanching generalized rash post-travel to Thailand.
- Differential includes viral exanthem (e.g., dengue, other arboviral infection), early systemic bacterial infection, and meningitis (less likely given absence of photophobia, neck stiffness, non-blanching rash, or focal deficits, but cannot be ruled out without exam).
- No ENT-specific pathology identified at present.

Plan:
- Urgent in-person assessment:
  • Patient advised to attend Babylon clinical hub for physical examination and possible labs “within the next few hours.”
  • If no appointment available, directed to attend hospital emergency department the same day.
- Safety-netting / escalation instructions:
  • Seek immediate medical attention (call emergency services / present to hospital) if any of the following develop: worsening headache, inability to tolerate light, neck stiffness, altered consciousness, non-blanching rash, breathing difficulty, throat swelling, or any rapid deterioration.
- Follow-up:
  • In-person GP/ENT review arranged urgently; further referral (e.g., infectious diseases, neurology) dependent on exam findings.
  • No specific medication changes at this stage; continue symptomatic relief with paracetamol/ibuprofen as needed unless contraindicated.
- Preventive / education:
  • No specific ENT avoidance advice required; advised general monitoring and early review.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected elements: objective vitals (temperature, pulse, BP, SpO₂); detailed visual assessment of rash; full neurologic exam; detailed medication dosages; past immunization history; availability of emergency contact or accompaniment.
• Internal conflicts: None noted.
• Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; no inaudible sections.
